hello.prompt: Create hello.py that prints exactly "Hello, world!" when run, plus a unittest test in test_hello.py that verifies that output.

battleship.prompt: Build a small single-player Battleship game served by a Node.js HTTP server with no npm dependencies. server.js starts the server on the port in the PORT environment variable (default 3000). GET / serves a playable HTML page titled "Battleship" where the player fires at a computer-placed fleet on a 10x10 grid. GET /api/new starts a game and returns JSON with a game id; POST /api/fire with JSON {"game": id, "row": r, "col": c} returns JSON with "result" set to "miss", "hit" or "sunk" and "gameOver" true once every ship is sunk. Keep the game rules in a module the server uses, and cover them with node:test tests under test/ that run with `node --test`.
checks: node --test > node-test.log 2>&1; rc=$?; grep -Eq '^(ℹ|#) pass [1-9]' node-test.log && [ $rc -eq 0 ]; r=$?; rm -f node-test.log; exit $r

PORT=39171 node server.js > server.log 2>&1 & pid=$!; ok=1; for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:39171/ -o page.html 2>/dev/null && ok=0 && break; sleep 0.5; done; [ $ok -eq 0 ] && grep -qi battleship page.html; rc=$?; kill $pid 2>/dev/null; rm -f page.html; exit $rc

PORT=39172 node server.js > server.log 2>&1 & pid=$!; for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:39172/api/new -o new.json 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.5; done; node -e 'const g=JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("new.json","utf8")); const id=g.game??g.id??g.gameId; if(id===undefined) process.exit(2); fetch("http://127.0.0.1:39172/api/fire",{method:"POST",headers:{"content-type":"application/json"},body:JSON.stringify({game:id,row:0,col:0})}).then(r=>r.json()).then(j=>process.exit(["miss","hit","sunk"].includes(j.result)?0:3)).catch(()=>process.exit(4))'; rc=$?; kill $pid 2>/dev/null; rm -f new.json; exit $rc
